problem: build_accessibility_score_breakdown (src/output/json/helpers.rs) computed summary.accessibility_score_breakdown[] with a scoring model of its own that shared nothing with AccessibilityScorer::calculate_score: flat severity weights 20/14/8/4 that existed nowhere else in the codebase, a `severity_weight * (1 + ln(occurrences))` accumulation, a per-area cap at 90 lost points, and fixed 'importance' weights (15/15/15/10/15/15/8/7) that the scorer knows nothing about. The breakdown therefore described a different quantity than the score it claimed to break down.
evidence: reports/example-audit.json generated 2026-09-19 (auditmysite v1.5.0) reported summary.accessibility_score = 20 while summary.accessibility_score_breakdown[] held Semantics 52, Forms 59, Keyboard 83, Focus management 86, Images / alternative text 70, ARIA 10, Heading structure 88, Landmarks / page structure 10, with weight_pct summing to 100 — a weighted average of 57.4 against a reported score of 20. `auditmysite report-lint` was clean on the same file: every existing check is formal (grade matches score, counts sum to totals) and none reconciled a breakdown with the value it breaks down. The degenerate case agreed and so hid the defect: reports/casoon-audit.json had 0 findings, every area 100, score 100.
expected: The breakdown must be derived from the scorer's own per-rule ScoreImpact penalties and the scorer's own global pipeline, and must account for exactly the points the score actually lost. Because diversity_factor, the sqrt compression above COMPRESSION_KNEE, apply_soft_floor and the critical/high score cap are non-linear and depend on the whole finding set, no weighting of per-area sub-scores can reproduce the headline number. The breakdown apportions the real loss (100 - accessibility_score) across areas by each area's share of the raw per-rule penalty, using largest-remainder rounding. Invariant: sum(estimated_lost_points) == 100 - accessibility_score. (Superseded in part by accessibility-score-components-two-axes: the per-area `score` that this entry first kept next to the lost points, as the area run through the scorer on its own, was itself a second axis and is gone since schema 2.2.)
counter_examples: A report with no findings must keep every area at 0 lost points and weight_pct 0 — there is no loss to apportion and no share to report; see breakdown_is_all_clean_when_there_are_no_findings.
